clue.text: Get former pupil to exercise right away

indicators.note: right is the letter R, and sending it away means it is struck out of the word before

parts.note: an old boy of a school
to train is to exercise or drill

explanation.surface: An instruction to make an old boy of the school go off and work out.
explanation.walkthrough: OB plus TRAIN with its R removed gives OBTAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain something is to acquire or come by it, a plain synonym of get.

clue.text: Poplar relation of East End sock-seller

indicators.note: Cockneys from London's East End traditionally drop their aitches, so the leading H goes

parts.note: a hosier sells socks and stockings

explanation.surface: A sock-seller from the East End turns out to be related to someone from Poplar, an East End district.
explanation.walkthrough: Poplar looks like the London district, which fits the East End surface, but here it is the tree: the osier is a willow, and willows and poplars belong to the same family.
explanation.definitionFit: The osier is a willow, and willows share a botanical family with poplars, making it a close kin of that tree.

clue.text: Piece of camping equipment found by river that's not initially recognised by girl

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word recognised is not wanted, so that letter is removed from the river

parts.note: the Trent is a major English river
a girl's name, short for Margaret

explanation.surface: Campers find a piece of kit by a riverbank that a girl fails to recognise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not initially recognised' removes the letter that starts the word recognised, which is R, from the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A tent peg is the spike driven into the ground to hold a tent's guy ropes, a standard item of camping kit.

clue.text: Bury boxing champ takes first of amphetamines among other things

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A boxing champion from the town of Bury is caught taking amphetamines, among other things.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury looks like the Lancashire town, but it is the verb meaning to lay in a grave.
explanation.definitionFit: Inter alia is the Latin phrase used in English to mean among other things.

clue.text: Keep in work during military takeover

indicators.note: something happening during an event falls within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a coup is a seizure of power by the army
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Prisoners are kept locked in while working during a military takeover.
explanation.definitionFit: To coop up is to confine someone in a small space, which is to keep them in.

clue.text: Frequently finding fellow gripped by books on space

indicators.note: being gripped means being held inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: the Old Testament, a collection of books
an en is a printer's space

explanation.surface: A man often finds himself absorbed in books about outer space.
explanation.walkthrough: An en is a printer's measure of space, half an em, a common crossword source of EN.
explanation.definitionFit: Often and frequently both mean many times or regularly; they are straightforward synonyms.

clue.text: Soldier needing extremely large protective device

explanation.surface: A soldier needs some very large piece of protective gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely large' looks like an instruction to take the outer letters of large, but extremely is SO and large is L.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasol is a sunshade, a device that shields a person from strong sunshine.

clue.text: Distributed tape with uncle showing peevish irritation

indicators.note: things distributed are spread about, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: An uncle handing out tape grumpily shows he is irritated.
explanation.definitionFit: Petulance is childish sulky bad temper, the same thing as peevish irritation.

clue.text: Grave bearing it seen in New York after archaeological excavation

indicators.note: after sends the city piece to follow the excavation, reversing the clue's order

parts.note: an archaeologist's excavation is a dig

indicators.note: something seen in a place is inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

explanation.surface: A grave bearing an inscription has turned up in New York after an archaeological dig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grave' looks like a burial noun in this archaeological scene, but it is the adjective serious, and 'Grave bearing' together is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dignity is a serious, composed manner, so a solemn bearing is a fair description of it.

clue.text: To repeat it time after time requires energy

parts.note: an era is a period of time
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Saying something over and over again takes a lot of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time after time' looks like a phrase meaning repeatedly, but it is two separate times: ERA, then T.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to do or say again, a formal synonym of the verb repeat.

clue.text: Sufficiently good to contend with Anita regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at steady intervals, so every other letter of the name is kept

explanation.surface: Someone is good enough to take on Anita on a regular basis.
explanation.definitionFit: Competent describes someone adequate or capable enough for a task, which is being sufficiently good.

clue.text: England, for instance, giving support to peacekeepers after about turn by the Queen

indicators.note: after places the peacekeepers behind the turned piece, against the order the clue reads
to turn the word means to flip it round so it reads the other way

parts.note: on can mean about, as in a book on birds
the United Nations deploys peacekeeping forces

explanation.surface: England is backing UN peacekeepers after a royal U-turn by the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: PROP, then ER, then ON turned round to NO, then UN. ER for Elizabeth Regina is a standard crossword Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: England is a name, and a name of a particular place or person is what grammar calls a proper noun; England is one example.

clue.text: Fish only found in an area of the Atlantic

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a flatfish prized for eating
second meaning: an adjective, the one and single
third meaning: a sea area named in the BBC Shipping Forecast, south-west of Cornwall

explanation.surface: A particular fish turns up only in one stretch of the Atlantic Ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: Three separate meanings strung together; the Shipping Forecast is the BBC radio bulletin that divides British waters into named sea areas, one of them Sole.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a flatfish, means single or exclusive as an adjective, and is the title of a sea area in the Shipping Forecast.

clue.text: Letters from Orange Lodge's financial backer

indicators.note: the answer is made of a run of consecutive letters lifted straight out of the words that follow

parts.note: a run of consecutive letters inside these words

explanation.surface: Correspondence from an Orange Lodge reveals who has been funding it.
explanation.walkthrough: An Orange Lodge is a branch of the Protestant Orange Order, prominent in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: An angel is the informal name for an investor who backs a venture, especially a theatre show.

clue.text: Change by turns every second

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a verb, to swap back and forth
second meaning: an adjective, every other one

explanation.walkthrough: 'Every second' reads like a measure of time, but it means every other one, as in alternate Tuesdays.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means switching back and forth repeatedly; as an adjective it describes every other item in a series.

clue.text: Get the better of Eric at the outset with story about new means of transportation

indicators.note: the story's letters wrap around the next piece

parts.note: to pip is to beat narrowly

indicators.note: the outset is the beginning, so only the name's opening letter is used

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story

explanation.surface: Someone beats Eric from the start by telling a tale about a new kind of transport.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipeline is a long run of pipes carrying oil, gas or water, which is a means of transporting them.

clue.text: Fellow looking into aims of TV quiz show

indicators.note: one who looks into something has his head inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to aim a gun is to point it

explanation.surface: A man investigates what a television quiz programme is trying to achieve.
explanation.walkthrough: Pointless is a BBC quiz show in which contestants try to find the answers fewest people gave.
explanation.definitionFit: Pointless is the title of a long-running BBC television quiz programme, so the clue gives an example.

clue.text: Begin to admit gangster needing wife to become committed in support

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the next pieces are placed inside

explanation.surface: A gangster is let in on condition that he brings his wife along to be a loyal supporter.
explanation.walkthrough: Al Capone is the crossword's usual gangster.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalwart is loyal and dependable, a firm backer of a cause, so committed in support fits.

clue.text: Extremely foolish for London's earliest university to have Brown back in charge

indicators.note: earliest points to the first letter of the city's name
going back means reading the word the other way round

explanation.surface: Having Gordon Brown back in charge of London's oldest university would be very foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: L, U, then TAN reversed as NAT, then IC.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunatic as an adjective means wildly irrational or absurd, which is extremely foolish.

clue.text: Last of tiles taken from unique fireplace

indicators.note: taken from means removed out of, so that letter is struck from the word that follows

parts.note: single means one of a kind

indicators.note: only the final letter of the following word is wanted

explanation.surface: The last of the tiles has been removed from a one-of-a-kind fireplace.
explanation.walkthrough: SINGLE loses its S.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingle is an old word for a hearth or open fire, as in inglenook, the corner by a fireplace.

clue.text: Yes uttered after German boy's inviting glance

indicators.note: uttered means spoken, so the word is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: aye is an old or dialect word for yes

explanation.surface: A German boy says yes after being given a come-hither look.
explanation.walkthrough: G and LAD come first; AYE spoken aloud gives EYE.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone the glad eye is an old idiom for flirting with a look, an inviting glance.

clue.text: Press club

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to smooth clothes with a heated appliance
second meaning: a golf club with an angled metal head

explanation.walkthrough: Press and club look like a journalists' club, but they are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for smoothing creases from fabric and also the name for a type of golf club.

clue.text: Press going to town after politician shows a stiffness of manner

indicators.note: after means the press piece and town follow the politician, not precede him

parts.note: to strain is to press, as when pushing hard

explanation.surface: The press heads into town to follow a politician who appears stiff and awkward.
explanation.walkthrough: Press appeared as a definition in the previous clue; here it supplies wordplay as the verb strain, to push hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Constraint can mean an inhibited, unnatural restraint in behaviour, which is a stiffness of manner.

clue.text: Worries about filling bag up

indicators.note: a filling sits inside something, so one piece goes within the other
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a sac is a bag or pouch

explanation.surface: Someone frets about stuffing a bag full.
explanation.definitionFit: Cares as a plural noun means anxieties or troubles, the same as worries.

clue.text: Interestingly unusual for Emma perhaps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an adjective for something new and different
second meaning: a noun, since Emma is a book by Jane Austen

explanation.walkthrough: Emma looks like a woman's name, but it is Jane Austen's book; perhaps flags it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means original and fresh; the noun is a long work of prose fiction, of which Austen's Emma is one.

clue.text: Land for grazing is beyond river

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Grazing land lies on the far side of the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A pasture is a field covered with grass where cattle and sheep feed.

clue.text: Warrant cards finally found in grass over towards the centre of Staveley

indicators.note: turned over means the grass word is read backwards
found in means sitting inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it
the middle of the place name is all that is taken

parts.note: the two central letters of the eight

explanation.surface: Police warrant cards turn up in long grass near the centre of Staveley.
explanation.walkthrough: Warrant looks like part of 'warrant cards', the police ID, but it is the verb alone. Staveley is a small town in Cumbria.
explanation.definitionFit: To warrant something is to merit or justify it, the same as to deserve it.

clue.text: Extremely sensitive after former copper has reason to justify offence

indicators.note: after puts the sensitive piece at the end, behind the former copper
extremely means at the extremes, so only the first and last letters of the next word are used

parts.note: the word's first and last letters

explanation.surface: A sensitive former police officer offers a reason to justify having taken offence.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper looks like a police officer, but it is the metal, with symbol CU.
explanation.definitionFit: An excuse is an explanation put forward to defend or pardon a fault or wrongdoing.

clue.text: Advisable to take arsenic too

parts.note: well can mean advisable, as in it would be well to wait

explanation.surface: Someone suggests that taking arsenic as well would be wise.
explanation.definitionFit: As well and too are interchangeable adverbs meaning in addition or also.
